title: Trends, Patterns & Indicators
promise: The map (trends, support, resistance) and the instruments (indicators) of technical analysis.
unlock: Tell an uptrend, a downtrend and a range from the swings
Draw trendlines and channels without forcing them
Use a moving average to pick which side to trade
Spot double tops, double bottoms and head and shoulders, then wait for the break
Read RSI and MACD without panicking
Build a clean chart where every tool answers a different question

questions.q: Over two months, a stock’s highs went $30, $33, $36. Its lows went $27, $29, $32. What’s the trend?
options: Up: higher highs and higher lows
Sideways: it keeps pulling back
Sideways: the lows are still close together
questions.why: Each high beats the last, and so does each low. Pullbacks along the way don’t make it a range.
questions.work: Highs $30 → $33 → $36. Lows $27 → $29 → $32. Each one higher than the last.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Price closes 1% below a 3-month rising trendline. What does that tell you?
options: Sell everything: the trend is over
Buy more: it’s a bargain now
A warning: watch the next highs and lows
questions.why: A break is a warning, not a signal. Price often slips under a line and climbs back.
questions.work: One close, 1% below the line. A lower high and a lower low would confirm the turn.

chart.label: A rising trendline; the last weekly close is about 1% below it

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: A stock trades at $40. Its 50-day moving average is $44 and falling. What does that suggest?
options: An uptrend: the average will pull it up
A downtrend: price is below a falling average
A buy signal: it’s cheap below its average
questions.why: Price below a falling average is what a downtrend looks like. Below the average doesn’t mean cheap, and the average follows price, not the other way around.

chart.label: Price at $40 below a falling 50-day average at $44

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: A double bottom: two lows at $20, middle high at $24. Price is now $23. Is it confirmed?
options: Yes: two lows at $20 are enough
Not yet: it needs a close above $24
Yes: price already bounced $3
questions.why: Two lows only show a range. The double bottom counts on a close above the $24 middle high, and $23 is still below it.
questions.work: Lows $20 and $20. Middle high $24. Now $23: still below $24.

chart.label: Two lows at $20, a middle high at $24, price now $23

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: A head and shoulders has its neckline at $80. Price closes at $78. What does that mean?
options: Confirmed, but it can still fail: use a stop
Nothing yet: it must fall to the target first
A buy: it’s near support
questions.why: A close below the neckline confirms the pattern. Patterns still fail often, so a confirmed break needs a stop.

chart.label: A head and shoulders; price closes at $78 below the $80 neckline

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: A stock in a strong uptrend has an RSI of 75. What is the most sensible read?
options: Sell now: it’s overbought
Short it: RSI must fall back to 50
Price is rising fast, and that can last
questions.why: RSI 75 says price rose fast, not that it must fall. Strong trends can stay overbought for weeks.

chart.label: A strong uptrend with RSI at 75

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: The MACD line crosses below its signal line. The stock has gone sideways for two months. How much weight should the cross get?
options: Little: in sideways markets most crosses go nowhere
A lot: it’s a clear sell signal
It means price will fall 10%
questions.why: When price goes sideways, the lines cross back and forth and most crosses go nowhere. A cross confirms a trend; it’s never a reason on its own.

chart.label: Two months sideways; the MACD line just crossed below its signal

questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: You use a 50-day average for the trend. Which pair adds the most new information?
options: A 20-day and a 100-day average
Support levels and volume
RSI and Stochastic
questions.why: More averages repeat the trend question, and RSI with Stochastic repeat one momentum view. Levels and volume answer new questions: where, and who’s behind it.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Over six weeks, a stock’s highs went $62, $58, $55. Its lows went $57, $53, $50. What’s the trend?
options: Up: it keeps bouncing back
Down: lower highs and lower lows
Sideways: the swings are about the same size
retry.why: Each high is lower than the last, and so is each low. The bounces along the way don’t change that.
retry.work: Highs $62 → $58 → $55. Lows $57 → $53 → $50. Each one lower than the last.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Price closed just under a rising trendline yesterday. Today the next swing low holds above the last one. What does that tell you?
options: The uptrend is over: sell now
The warning hasn’t been confirmed: no lower low yet
Trendlines stop working after a break
retry.why: A break is a warning. The trend turns only when the swings turn: a lower high and a lower low. A higher low means the uptrend still holds.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: A stock trades at $75. Its 50-day moving average is $70 and rising. What does that suggest?
options: A downtrend: it must fall back to $70
An uptrend: price is above a rising average
Nothing: you need a 200-day too
retry.why: Price above a rising average is what an uptrend looks like. It doesn’t say how long it lasts.

chart.label: Price at $75 above a rising 50-day average at $70

retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: A double top: two peaks at $60, middle low at $54. Price closes at $53. What does that mean?
options: Confirmed: it closed below the $54 middle low
Not yet: it must fall to $48 first
Nothing: two peaks never matter
retry.why: A close through the middle point confirms it, and $53 is below the $54 middle low. The rough target, about $48, is only a guide.
retry.work: Middle low $54. Close $53: below it. Height $60 − $54 = $6, so a rough target near $48.

chart.label: Two peaks at $60 and a close at $53, below the $54 middle low

retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Left shoulder $40, head $46, right shoulder $41. The neckline is $37 and price is at $38. Is the pattern confirmed?
options: Yes: the right shoulder has formed
Not yet: it needs a close below $37
Yes: price is falling from the shoulder
retry.why: The shape alone is only a hint. The pattern counts on a close below the $37 neckline, and $38 is still above it.

chart.label: Shoulders at $40 and $41, head at $46, neckline $37, price now $38

retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: A stock in a strong uptrend has had an RSI above 70 for three weeks. Your friend says it must fall now. What’s the sensible read?
options: It must fall: three weeks is too long
Strong trends can stay overbought for weeks
Short it until RSI hits 50
retry.why: Above 70 says price rose fast, not that it must fall. In strong uptrends RSI can stay up there for weeks.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: A stock has gone sideways for three months. The MACD line crosses above its signal line. How much weight should the cross get?
options: A lot: it’s a clear buy signal
Little: in sideways markets most crosses go nowhere
It means price will rise 10%
retry.why: Sideways markets make the lines cross back and forth, and most crosses go nowhere. A cross confirms a trend; it’s never a reason on its own.

chart.label: Three months sideways; the MACD line just crossed above its signal

retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: You use a 50-day average for the trend and RSI for momentum. Which addition brings new information?
options: Stochastic
A 100-day average
Volume on the move
retry.why: Stochastic repeats RSI, and another average repeats the trend. Volume answers a new question: who’s behind the move.

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · What a trend really is
refresher.text: Compare each swing with the last. Higher highs and higher lows: uptrend. Lower highs and lower lows: downtrend. No new highs or lows: sideways.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · Trendlines and channels
refresher.text: Draw the line under at least two rising lows. A break is a warning, not a signal: wait for lower highs and lower lows.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · Moving averages: the smoothed trend
refresher.text: Above a rising average: uptrend. Below a falling one: downtrend. The average lags, so it confirms the trend; it doesn’t predict it.

refresher.title: Lesson 4 · Double tops and double bottoms
refresher.text: Two failed tries at a level are only a range until price closes through the middle point. No break, no pattern.

refresher.title: Lesson 5 · Head and shoulders
refresher.text: The pattern counts only on a close through the neckline. Patterns fail often, so a confirmed break still needs a stop.

refresher.title: Lesson 6 · RSI: overbought isn’t a sell signal
refresher.text: RSI measures speed. Above 70 means price rose fast, not that it must fall: strong trends stay overbought for weeks.

refresher.title: Lesson 7 · MACD in plain words
refresher.text: MACD crosses lag, and in a sideways market they flip back and forth. A cross confirms a trend; it’s never a reason on its own.

refresher.title: Lesson 8 · Confluence over clutter
refresher.text: Indicators built from the same prices repeat each other. Real confluence is trend, level and volume agreeing: three different questions.
